feedback.problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{x}{2-{x}^{4}}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{4}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{x}{2-{x}^{4}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{x}{{x}^{4}})}{(\frac{2}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}{(\frac{2}{{x}^{4}}-1)} \\  & =\frac{0}{0-1} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$ is $y=0.$
